newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts gain with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts gain with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Thursday in a moderate session, with talk of firmer cash prices and bullish inventory data keeping front months in positive territory, industry sources said.
September firmed 1.6 cents to close at $2.177 per million British thermal units. October settled 2.1 cents higher at $2.176. Others ended mixed, with 1999s losing ground.
"We don't have a lot of heat and it was surprising how many people were looking for gas," said one trader, noting weekend prices for Henry Hub looked strong today.
Most agreed Wednesday's unexpectedly-light weekly U.S. gas stock build also helped set the stage today for higher numbers, particularly with the gap to 1994 and 1995 storage levels steadily growing.

But technical traders noted September, which briefly broke resistance today at $2.20, failed to close above it, leaving the market range bound. They saw next resistance at the $2.27 double top. Near-supprt was pegged in the $2.15-2.16 area and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.10 area. More important support was expected at $2.08 and then at last week's low of $2.045.

Warmer Midwest and Northeast weather is expected into the weekend, but cooler air is forecast for early next week. Temperatures in Florida and Texas are expected to stay close to normal for the period, Weather Services Corp said.

In the cash Thursday, early-August Gulf Coast gas firmed a few cents to about the $2.20 level. August Midcon gained almost five cents to the $2.12-2.15 area. New York city gate gas held relatively steady in the low-$2.40s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose 1.1 cents to $2.222. NYMEX said 38,548 contracts traded, up from Wednesday's revised tally of 24,435.

On the KCBT, September finished unchanged at $2.065, while deferreds ended narrowly mixed. The East/West spread widened by 1.6 cents to 11.2 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 261 contracts traded, down sharply from Wednesday's total of 1,524.
